newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela stands by controversial mining project.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela stands by controversial mining project.

text.p: Top Venezuelan officials reiterated on Tuesday their intention to push ahead with a plan to turn a huge forestry reserve into one of the largest gold producing areas in Latin America.

Ministers and regional officials met in the regional capital Ciudad Bolivar, 550 miles (880 km) southeast of Caracas, to hand out the first nine concessions to mining cooperatives to work in the Imataca forest reserve.
Officials said granting mining permits to cooperatives and large foreign companies would protect Imataca from the uncontrolled activities of up to 50,000 illegal miners.

According to government estimates, a development of the Imataca reserve -- which is about the size of El Salvador -- could bring the country $900 million per year in taxes and royalties and make Venezuela a top 10 world gold producer.
The plan to develop the reserve has met sharp protests from environmentalists, indigenous groups and legislators who say the government has exaggerated the problem of illegal mining.
"Of course this (project) is not a panacea," Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said, adding that the government would need to increase security in the region to clamp down on illegal miners.
